title: The year everyone tried to sell to Generation X
lede: OK arrived in a [soft drink market](/category/consumer/) that had stopped growing and a youth market that large companies were studying closely.

blocks.title: A slow market and a crowd of small rivals
blocks.body:
The New York Times described the American carbonated-beverage market in April 1994 as “lackluster,” and read OK as a move against the independent brands in “the growing market for alternative beverages.”[^4] Time quoted the editor of Beverage World: Coke and Pepsi had traditionally let smaller companies innovate, and “now Coke is becoming an innovator too.”[^6]

Coca-Cola launched Fruitopia the same year as a rival to Snapple, and a Sprite campaign, “Obey Your Thirst,” that Time said “pointedly refuses to overpromise.”[^13][^6] A year earlier its product list had included Tab Clear, its clear cola from the year of [Crystal Pepsi](/crystal-pepsi/); by the 1994 report that was gone.[^2][^1]
